content:
Winter weather is arriving across seven U.S. states on Monday, Oct. 26, as falling temperatures bring snow to the Rockies and northern Plains, while a separate storm threatens Alaska with up to 16 inches of snow and wind gusts reaching 55 mph, according to a report published Monday morning.

The biggest concern is Alaska, where National Weather Service warnings extend into Monday night. Farther south, Colorado, Wyoming, Montana, Nebraska, South Dakota, and North Dakota face varying chances of early-season snow, including a potentially messy Monday around the Black Hills.

The NOAA Weather Prediction Center identifies the Black Hills and portions of northwestern South Dakota and south-central North Dakota as areas where snow could accumulate Monday. AccuWeather Senior Meteorologist Bob Smerbeck warned the Black Hills could receive several inches, while the National Weather Service's Rapid City forecast is more restrained for the city itself, projecting less than half an inch Monday.

The distinction matters for travelers: mountain snowfall totals should not be mistaken for expected accumulation in nearby cities. Temperatures remain marginal for accumulation, meaning snow falling during warmer daylight hours may struggle to stick, while snow arriving before sunrise or after sunset has a better chance of accumulating.

For Webb County readers, the storm brings no direct local impact, but it is a factor for anyone traveling to or through the Rockies, the northern Plains, or Alaska this week, or expecting deliveries and flights routed through those regions. Conditions should be checked with the National Weather Service before travel.

Sources:

  • Men's Journal, "Winter Storm Hits 7 US States Monday as Up to 16 Inches of Snow, 55 MPH Winds Loom," Oct. 26, 2026
  • NOAA Weather Prediction Center, cited by Men's Journal
  • National Weather Service Rapid City, cited by Men's Journal

title: Winter storm hits seven states Monday, with up to 16 inches of snow and 55-mph winds in Alaska
